member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Configuration.DemoWorkspaceLayout
member.summary: Shared, host-agnostic rules for the isolated Meridian demo workspace that the --seed-demo / --reset-demo CLI verbs and the --demo serve mode operate on.

remarks.para: The demo workspace is a dedicated, clearly-named data root nested one level under the active data root ({dataRoot}/demo-workspace). Every seeded, durable store is rooted here, so seeding can never write into — and --reset-demo can never delete — a non-demo root.
This type is intentionally dependency-free and pure so the same isolation and guard rules are enforced identically by the host CLI, the shared startup bootstrapper, the seeder, and tests.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Configuration.SymbolConfig
member.summary:
Configuration for a subscribed symbol and how to build its IB contract.
Notes for preferred shares on IB: - Preferreds are usually represented as SecType=STK with a LocalSymbol like "PCG PRA" or "PCG PR A". - To avoid ambiguity, set LocalSymbol explicitly when possible.
Notes for options: - Set SecurityType to "OPT" and provide Strike, Right, and LastTradeDateOrContractMonth. - For index options (SPX, NDX, RUT), set OptionStyle to European and InstrumentType to IndexOption. - For equity options, OptionStyle defaults to American.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.CanonicalSymbol
member.summary: Zero-cost value object representing a normalized, canonical market instrument symbol. Distinct from (the raw provider symbol) to prevent accidental use of un-normalized symbols where a canonical symbol is expected and vice-versa.
member.remarks: Use this type wherever a symbol has been through the canonicalization pipeline (e.g. "AAPL.US" from Stooq → "AAPL" as the canonical form). The compiler will then enforce that raw and canonical symbols are never silently interchanged. Equality and comparison are case-insensitive; values are stored in uppercase.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.Enums.LiquidityProfile
member.summary: Classification of expected trading activity for a symbol. Determines monitoring thresholds for gap detection, completeness scoring, SLA freshness, and anomaly detection.

member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.Enums.LiquidityProfile.High
member.summary: High liquidity - large cap equities, major ETFs, FX majors. Continuous quoting, hundreds of trades per minute. Gap threshold ~60s, expected ~1000+ events/hour.

member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.Enums.LiquidityProfile.Normal
member.summary: Normal liquidity - mid-cap equities, sector ETFs, active options. Regular but not constant activity. Gap threshold ~120s, expected ~200 events/hour.

member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.Enums.LiquidityProfile.Low
member.summary: Low liquidity - small-cap stocks, less active options, single-stock futures. Trades may be minutes apart during quiet periods. Gap threshold ~600s, expected ~20 events/hour.

member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.Enums.LiquidityProfile.VeryLow
member.summary: Very low liquidity - OTC stocks, thinly-traded options, illiquid bonds. Trades may be 10+ minutes apart; wide spreads are normal. Gap threshold ~1800s, expected ~5 events/hour.

member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.Enums.LiquidityProfile.Minimal
member.summary: Minimal activity - deep OTC, far out-of-money options, exotic instruments. May have fewer than a handful of trades per day. Gap threshold ~3600s, expected ~1 event/hour.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.IPositionSnapshotStore
member.summary: Provides crash-safe persistence for per-account portfolio snapshots. Implementations must follow the WAL pattern (ADR-007) and respect the LifecyclePolicyEngine tiered-storage rules (ADR-002).

member.name: M:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.IPositionSnapshotStore.SaveSnapshotAsync(Meridian.Contracts.Domain.AccountSnapshotRecord,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Persists an account snapshot with the same atomic equivalence/conflict semantics as . This retained compatibility method does not expose whether an equivalent retry was skipped.

member.name: M:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.IPositionSnapshotStore.SaveSnapshotConditionallyAsync(Meridian.Contracts.Domain.AccountSnapshotRecord,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Atomically persists an account snapshot using the logical identity of run, account, exact owner scope, and UTC . An equivalent retry must be a no-op; a different payload at the same identity must throw . The check and append must be serialized for concurrent writers to the same durable partition. Implementations must resolve "latest" by the greatest value rather than physical append order.
member.remarks: The default implementation fails closed so an older store implementation cannot silently provide non-atomic behavior to a caller that requires a conditional append.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.Models.SessionStats
member.summary: Per-symbol intraday session statistics derived from observed trades. Captures the conventional "today" reference points a watchlist or quote display needs: open, high, low, last, total volume, and a volume-weighted average price.
member.remarks: The session boundary is the calendar date in UTC. When a trade arrives whose UTC date differs from , the collector resets the state and starts a new session anchored to the new date's first observed trade. This keeps the model honest in the absence of an exchange-local trading calendar; consumers that need a different anchor (e.g. America/New_York midnight) can plug in a different collector.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Domain.ProviderSymbol
member.summary: Zero-cost value object pairing a provider identifier with a raw, provider-specific symbol string. Represents the symbol exactly as the upstream provider exposes it — before any canonicalization is applied.

remarks.para: Use at provider boundaries (ingestion adapters, backfill clients, symbol-search providers) where the raw, vendor-specific ticker must be carried alongside the provider identity. Examples:

item.description: Stooq yields "AAPL.US" for the symbol later canonicalized to "AAPL".
Polygon yields "X:BTCUSD" for a crypto pair.
IB yields "AAPL" directly, but provider context is still needed for resolution.

remarks.para: The three symbol types form a strict hierarchy:

item.description: — raw canonical ticker, provider-independent (e.g. after normalization).
— fully resolved, system-wide canonical symbol (e.g. after the canonicalization pipeline).

remarks.para: Equality is case-insensitive on both and fields.

member.summary: Zero-cost value object representing a raw, provider-independent market instrument symbol. This is the "Symbol (raw)" type in the typed symbol hierarchy. Prevents accidental interchange of symbols with other string-typed IDs (e.g. or ).

remarks.para: The three symbol types form a strict hierarchy:

item.description: — raw, provider-scoped ticker (before mapping, e.g. "AAPL.US" from Stooq).

member.summary: Origin of the figures this posting carries. Defaults to . member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Ledger.LedgerPostingKindDto.ClosingEntry
member.summary: Period-close closing entries. Produced only by the governed period-close workflow after human approval, these are the sanctioned exception to the closed-period posting bar: they finalize the period being closed by zeroing temporary accounts and rolling net income to retained earnings, so the posting guard permits them into soft- and hard-closed periods.

member.name: M:Meridian.Contracts.Ledger.LedgerCurrencyRounding.RoundCurrency(System.Decimal)

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Ledger.LedgerToleranceConstants
member.summary: Shared numeric tolerances for ledger and accounting equality comparisons. member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Ledger.LedgerToleranceConstants.Balance
member.summary: Absolute epsilon for treating a ledger balance as reconciled — for example total debits versus total credits. Guards against false imbalances introduced by independent decimal rounding paths.

member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Ledger.LedgerToleranceConstants.Allocation
member.summary: Absolute epsilon for treating an allocation or apportionment total as fully distributed (for example partnership waterfall and investor allocations). Shares 's value but is named distinctly so the two thresholds can diverge later without reintroducing duplication.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Operations.DataProvenance
member.summary: Origin classification carried by any figure or read model that can be produced from something other than real operational data. The point of the signal is fail-closed honesty: no operator, on either client, may mistake simulated, seeded, or sample output for real data. Every read model that can originate from non-real data carries this signal and propagates it outward; surfaces that only ever show real data may default to .

member.summary: Real operational data captured from a durable production source.

member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Operations.DataProvenance.Simulated
member.summary: Deterministically generated by a simulation, paper, or backtest path (e.g. a synthetic streaming source or a shadow-book valuation). Numbers move, but none of it is real.

member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Operations.DataProvenance.Seeded
member.summary: Deterministically seeded fixture data shipped so a new operator can explore the product without credentials (e.g. demo-mode market snapshots).

member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Operations.DataProvenance.Sample
member.summary: Illustrative sample or placeholder data with no operational meaning.

member.summary: Shared helpers for reasoning about and rendering a signal. Kept in the contracts layer so both clients, the API endpoints, and the DI policy render one label.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Pipeline.IngestionJob
member.summary: Unified ingestion job state machine that applies to both realtime and historical flows. Implements a single contract for all ingestion workload types, ensuring consistent status tracking, checkpoint semantics, and retry behavior.
member.remarks:
State transitions: Draft → Queued → Running → Paused → Completed | Failed | Cancelled
Resume behavior by workload type: Realtime: restart from latest stream + gap-fill window Historical: resume from last committed bar cursor (checkpoint token)

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.SecurityMaster.DayCountConventions
member.summary: The single canonical day-count engine for Meridian's fixed-income math. Every accrual, coupon, premium/discount amortization, cost-basis relief, and read-model preview path MUST route through this type so the same bond produces the same day-count fraction everywhere — otherwise GL postings and cost-basis relief silently fail to tie. The F# DayCount module delegates here as well, so there is exactly one 30/360 (and Actual/Actual) implementation across the C# and F# lanes.

remarks.para: Convention semantics follow the ISDA 2006 definitions, §4.16:

item.description: 30/360 US (Bond Basis, §4.16(f)): D1 of 31 becomes 30; D2 of 31 becomes 30 only when D1 is (already) 30 or 31. No February end-of-month rule — that variant (30/360 US NASD/EOM) is intentionally not applied, matching every existing Meridian call site.
30E/360 (Eurobond, §4.16(g)): D1 and D2 of 31 both become 30, unconditionally.

30E/360 ISDA (§4.16(h)): D1/D2 become 30 when they are the last day of their month (February included). The §4.16(h) carve-out — D2 stays at February's true end when the end date is the instrument's maturity — needs maturity context, so the dedicated overload exposes it.
Business/252: needs a business-day calendar; use the overload with a calendar predicate. Without one it degrades to Actual/365.

remarks.para: All arithmetic is end-to-end; no intermediates, so fractions are exact and reproducible across runtimes.

member.summary: Parses a raw convention string (e.g. "30/360", "30E/360", "ACT/365", "Act/Act ICMA", "NL/365", "BUS/252", "Thirty360", "ActualActualISDA") into a . Never throws: blank or unrecognized input returns .

member.summary: Converts a structured economic-terms payload (, the nested maturity/coupon/discount/accrual/payment shape) into the flat legacy asset-specific-terms shape () that the mapping, resolver, and projection paths read. member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.SecurityMaster.SecurityAssetTermsSchema
member.summary: The single declarative source of truth for the flat, per-asset-class asset-specific-terms field contract. Historically the same field/type table was hand-maintained three times — the F# serialize side (Interop.SecurityMaster.assetSpecificTermsJson), the C# deserialize side (SecurityMasterMapping.ToSecurityKind), and the relational projection decoders in the Postgres store — which let them silently drift (e.g. the projection store reading a nested coupon object the serializer never wrote, so bond coupon columns landed null). This table names each class's fields once so those codec surfaces can be validated against a single contract instead of against each other. It mirrors the data-driven pattern already proven by AssetClassValidatorRegistry.
member.remarks: Keys and types are taken from the authoritative serialize contract (the F# SecurityKind term records). Fields carrying nested/collection shapes are typed or ; their inner shapes are not enumerated here.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.SecurityMaster.SecurityTermReader
member.summary: Shared low-level reader for probing economic-term JSON by case-insensitive key aliases. Centralizes the value-coercion rules (string/number/bool → string, number/string → decimal, string → date) so cash-flow and obligation projections resolve terms identically instead of each carrying its own copy of the probing helpers. member.summary: Resolves a security's raw term JSON into . member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Tenancy.IFundProfileTenancyRegistry
member.summary:
Authoritative registry mapping a fund profile to its owning tenant/company — the storage-enforced source of truth for fund-scoped tenant isolation (security backlog SEC-005).
Once a fund profile is bound to a tenant, data keyed by that fund (strategy runs, ledger books, report packs) must only be served to callers in the owning tenant. Ownership is established on first authoritative use under a tenant scope (trust-on-first-use); the first owner wins and is never silently reassigned. Under a single-company-per-deployment runtime every fund binds to the one tenant, so nothing is ever foreign and behavior is unchanged.

member.name: M:Meridian.Contracts.Tenancy.IFundProfileTenancyRegistry.BindAsync(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Claims for the given tenant/company if it is currently unbound, then returns the effective owner. Idempotent and first-owner-wins: a fund already bound to a different tenant is left unchanged and that existing owner is returned, so the caller can compare it to detect a foreign fund.

member.summary: Resolves the owning tenant/company for a fund profile, or null when it is unbound.

member.summary: True when the caller's tenant may use the fund: it is unbound (unknown) or bound to the caller. False only when the fund is bound to a different tenant. A read-only check — it never binds.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Tenancy.IFundScopeTenantAccessor
member.summary:
Resolves the caller's server-side tenant for the current ambient scope (e.g. the active HTTP request), so storage can apply SEC-005 slice 4c-ii tenant read predicates without threading a caller-tenant argument through every read method and intermediate service.
Returns null when there is no tenant in scope — a non-request/background caller, or the single-company-per-deployment runtime where the legacy tenantless admin profile has no company. A null result is the fail-open signal: reads are not tenant-scoped and every row passes, matching the deployment-boundary posture. The web layer supplies an -backed implementation; the storage layer depends only on this abstraction (no ASP.NET Core coupling).

member.name: M:Meridian.Contracts.Tenancy.IFundScopeTenantAccessor.ResolveCallerTenant
member.summary: The caller's resolved tenant id for the current scope, or null when none is in scope (fail-open).

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Tenancy.FundScopedWriteTenantDecision
member.summary: SEC-005 slice 4c-iii decision for a fund-scoped write request: whether a session with no server-resolved tenant may create or evaluate fund-scoped accounting artifacts.
member.remarks: This is a deliberate, deployment-gated contract change: today the legacy MDC_USERNAME admin profile has no CompanyId, so its resolved tenant is null and it can write in the global namespace. Requiring a tenant would 403 that supported single-company session, so enforcement is off by default and rolled out detection-first — a tenantless write is logged (so operators can see whether any real deployment still relies on it) but allowed until a deployment opts in. The decision is isolated here so the three-way branch is unit-testable without spinning up the pipeline.

member.summary: Tenantless caller, enforcement off: record a detection warning, then proceed.

member.name: F:Meridian.Contracts.Tenancy.FundScopedWriteTenantDecision.Deny
member.summary: Tenantless caller, enforcement on: refuse the write (fail closed).

member.summary: Pure decision for the SEC-005 4c-iii fund-scoped write tenant gate.

member.name: M:Meridian.Contracts.Tenancy.FundScopedWriteTenantGate.Decide(System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: A caller with a resolved tenant is always allowed. A tenantless caller is denied only when enforcement is enabled; otherwise it is allowed but flagged for detection.

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Tenancy.TenantReadPredicate
member.summary: SEC-005 slice 4c-ii read-predicate decision. Centralizes the rule for whether a fund-scoped read should filter by the stamped tenant_id column, and the SQL fragment that does so, so the fail-open branch is unit-testable without a database and is shared across every fund-scoped store (ledger, operations-continuity, …) rather than re-derived per store.
member.remarks:
The Postgres stores' integration suites are skipped in CI (no database), so an over-filtering regression — a predicate wrongly applied to a tenantless caller, or a normalization mismatch — would otherwise ship uncaught and make legitimate single-company data vanish. Keeping the decision here lets the highest-risk branch (tenantless caller ⇒ no filter) be proven in CI.
Semantics: a row is visible when its tenant_id IS NULL (unbound/legacy — fail-open) OR equals the caller's tenant. The predicate is emitted ONLY when the caller has a resolved tenant; a tenantless caller (single-company deployment, or the legacy tenantless admin profile) gets no predicate at all, so every row passes and behavior is identical under one-company-per-deployment. The comparison uses lower(trim(...)) on both sides to match the write-side stamp and (trimmed, case-insensitive).

member.name: T:Meridian.Contracts.Workstation.PublishSecurityMasterRevisionRequest
member.summary:
Publishes an approved revision (durable append + downstream propagation).
The downstream restatement impact is scoped to the fund captured on the draft revision (the fund the edit was made under, if any). Publish deliberately carries no caller-supplied fund scope, so a publisher cannot resolve impact for a fund the operator did not edit under. Publish-time re-scoping and cross-fund (multi-held) expansion are a separate slice gated on tenant-scoped holdings discovery.
